source.author: verg
source.text: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto vi superum saevae memorem Iunonis ob iram; multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem, inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum, Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.
source.text_original: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris / Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit / litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto / vi superum saevae memorem Iunonis ob iram; / multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem, / inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum, / Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.
source.text_english: I sing of arms and the man, who first from the shores of Troy, an exile by fate, came to Italy and the Lavinian shores, much tossed about on land and on the deep by force of the gods above, on account of the mindful wrath of cruel Juno; and also much he suffered in war, until he should found a city and bring his gods to Latium, whence the Latin race, the Alban fathers, and the walls of lofty Rome.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ille ubi se mediae per scuta virosque carinae intulit, ardenti Aesonides retinacula ferro abscidit; haut aliter saltus vastataque pernix venator cum lustra fugit dominoque timentem urget equum, teneras compressans pectore tigres, quas astu rapuit pavido, dum saeva relictis mater in adverso catulis venatur Amano.
reuse.text_original: ille ubi se mediae per scuta virosque carinae / intulit, ardenti Aesonides retinacula ferro / abscidit; haut aliter saltus vastataque pernix / venator cum lustra fugit dominoque timentem / urget equum, teneras compressans pectore tigres, / quas astu rapuit pavido, dum saeva relictis / mater in adverso catulis venatur Amano.
reuse.text_english: When he had plunged himself amid the shields and men of the middle deck, the son of Aeson with burning iron cut the moorings; no otherwise, when a nimble hunter, with the glades laid waste, flees the lairs and drives on his frightened horse, pressing the tender tigers against his breast, which he had snatched by craft from the terrified mother, while the savage mother hunts after her abandoned cubs on the opposite Amanus.
